subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: For legacy primary-key values that collide only after required BLOB/TEXT normalization, should OpenClaw fail with a documented backup-and-repair workflow, or should Doctor offer a maintainer-approved deterministic remediation?
rationale: Selecting which conflicting persisted row, if any, may be retained is an irreversible user-data policy decision; source-level mechanics cannot safely choose that contract.

options.title: Fail closed with supported recovery
options.body: Keep the transactional failure, make the diagnostic accurately describe the required backup/manual repair path, and document it as the no-data-loss default.

options.title: Add deterministic Doctor remediation
options.body: Define and test an explicit collision-resolution policy in Doctor only after maintainers accept which records may be retained or quarantined.

options.title: Defer normalization for collisions
options.body: Leave affected tables non-STRICT until a future migration can preserve both identities under a maintainer-approved data model.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with supported recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the transactional failure, make the diagnostic accurately describe the required backup/manual repair path, and document it as the no-data-loss default.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied merged SQLite migration work is the direct provenance for the behavior and recovery boundary under review.
